result: the registration of the mammalian between-gene test, written before any RNA value was read

registration.question: The domain rule attributes a non-coding element to a gene. Between genes, where no rule can name the gene whose body the element sits in, does the gene with the nearest 5' end inside the element's boundary-delimited domain match the element's own tissue more often than the gene with the nearest 5' end on the chromosome? Two invertebrates DISAGREE about exactly this stratum -- the worm's domain rule is ahead by +3.73 points [+2.79, +4.74] on 2,335 between-gene elements and still ahead at +4.47 [+3.16, +5.78] after its own outron exclusion, while the fly's is +0.12 [-0.25, +0.61] on 3,265 brain elements, no difference detected -- and NOBODY HAS ASKED A MAMMAL. This is that question in the mouse.
registration.why_a_mammal: the fly's lead appears only where a host gene CAN be named (on all 10,052 distal elements the gene-structure rule is ahead of the boundary rule by -2.25 [-2.88, -1.66]), which is consistent with the fly's lead coming from host-gene transcription rather than regulation. The worm's lead survives where no host can be named. A mammal has 100 times the worm's intergenic space per gene, so whichever pattern it shows is the informative one.
registration.stop_list_of_2026_09_27: read, not ignored. 'No more biosamples: 1.1 needs its readings to mean what their names say' has as its subject the HUMAN reader's 13 biosamples, READER_TERMS in genomeos/genome/context_evidence.py. This lane adds none, names none and widens none. A MOUSE TISSUE SOURCE IS NOT A HUMAN READER BIOSAMPLE, as lane-flysource recorded for its fly source (docs/SIMPLER-GENOMES.md section 11).

boundary_set.primary: Bonev et al. 2017 (Cell 171:557-572.e24, DOI 10.1016/j.cell.2017.09.043, GEO GSE96107), Table S2 'Genomic Coordinates and Compartment Identity of the Topological Domains in Different Cell Types': the authors' own insulation-score domain call on mm10, read as the domain edges. The primary sheet is `ncx NPC` -- neural progenitors FACS-purified from EMBRYONIC NEOCORTEX, in vivo -- 2,398 domains. The other four sheets and three ENCODE e14.5 CTCF sets are beside
boundary_set.primary_licence: CC BY 4.0, verbatim from the article's front matter: 'This is an open access article under the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)'
boundary_set.primary_method: the authors' own, verbatim: 'The insulation score was computed ... at 1Kb resolution within a region of +/- 250Kb ... Domain boundaries were then defined as the local 2Kb maxima in regions, where the insulation score is above the 90% quantile of the genome-wide distribution. Boundaries within 10Kb of each other were merged and only boundaries, which were detected in at least 3 biological replicates, were retained. Domains shorter than 50Kb were discarded.' No caller and no threshold is chosen here
boundary_set.what_a_boundary_is_here: Bonev's domains are read as their edges -- every domain start and end, deduplicated -- which is the only conversion and has no parameter. The three ENCODE e14.5 CTCF sets reported beside take every conservative-IDR peak as a boundary, which is the brief's CTCF option and not a Hi-C domain call. 4D Nucleome's 110 mm10 boundary BEDs are NOT used: they are DCIC-pipeline calls rather than author calls, the portal requires a login, and the portal states no licence
boundary_set.why_this_one: it is the only author-called mouse Hi-C domain set found that is distributed in mm10 (so no liftover), states a licence in prose (CC BY 4.0), and was measured in EMBRYONIC tissue rather than a cell line. Of its five sheets, `ncx NPC` is the in-vivo progenitor population of the developing neocortex, the closest of the five to this panel's stage and to three of its twelve tissues. Section 11 registered its stage gap -- 2-3 h fly embryos against larval-to-adult brain elements -- as the price of a large enough population, and named a tissue-matched registration as the first thing that should follow; here the boundaries and the elements are both embryonic mouse.
what_was_searched_and_rejected: Gorkin et al. 2020 (Nature 583:744), the ENCODE mouse developmental matrix this panel's accessibility and RNA come from, publishes NO TAD or boundary table and generated no Hi-C: its own TADs are borrowed from Dixon et al. 2012 mESC. Its `d-TAC` is developmental transposase-accessible chromatin, not a TAD

Dixon et al. 2012 (Nature 485:376, GSE35156), 2,200 mESC domains at 40-kb bins, is mm9 and would need a liftover; its article states no licence, and its supplementary legends could not be read from the 6.3 MB SI PDF, so which table holds the domains is inference rather than a read statement. Not used

Vietri Rudan et al. 2015 (Cell Rep 10:1297, GSE65126) is mm10 adult liver but deposits only 50-kb interaction matrices; its Table S1 is 'Genomic Regions of Interest' and not a domain list. No author-called domain table exists
Nora et al. 2017 (Cell 169:930, GSE98671) deposits a raw tar and 5C primers; no boundary or domain table, and no CC licence is stated
Rao et al. 2014 (Cell 159:1665, GSE63525) does publish 2,927 Arrowhead contact domains for CH12-LX, but that is a B-lymphoblast CELL LINE and the coordinates are mm9

ENCODE serves no TAD or boundary file for any organism (0 files of output type 'topologically associated domains'). Its 105 mm10 `contact domains` bedpe files are Arrowhead calls on a 5-kb grid with a median length near 130 kb -- sub-TAD scale -- and ENCODE has NO embryonic or fetal mouse Hi-C at all, so none is tissue-matched to this panel
4D Nucleome has 110 mm10 boundary BEDs, but they are DCIC-pipeline calls and not author calls, the portal requires a login to download, and the portal states no licence anywhere
beside_deciding_nothing: Bonev's other four sheets on the same elements: `ncx CN` (2,307 domains, cortical neurons of embryonic neocortex, in vivo), `ES` (2,712, in vitro), `NPC` (2,522, in vitro) and `CN` (2,442, in vitro). None is dropped and none is chosen on an outcome

ENCODE CTCF ChIP-seq, embryonic day 14.5 -- the panel's own stage -- conservative IDR thresholded peaks on mm10: LIVER (ENCSR397RHW, ENCFF123IQA) and LUNG (ENCSR677SIH, ENCFF558ZIE), both of which are among the panel's twelve tissues, and BRAIN (ENCSR000CEH, ENCFF756OJJ), a tissue that is the union of three of them. These three are EVERY CTCF ChIP-seq experiment ENCODE has released at e14.5
boundary_set.bin: 500 bp (250 bp each side), carried verbatim from simpler_flynode and NOT retuned for the mouse: a gene's 5' end inside either flanking boundary's bin counts as inside the domain

registration.node: simpler_flysource.boundary_rule, unchanged: an element's domain runs from the boundary at or left of its midpoint to the next boundary right of it, or to the chromosome end; a gene is in the domain when its 5' end lies there or inside either boundary's bin; the rule names the in-domain gene with the nearest 5' end, and falls back to nearest TSS when the domain holds no 5' end. No new node is proposed here.
registration.population: THE BETWEEN-GENE ELEMENTS: ENCODE SCREEN mm10 cCREs whose SCREEN class is not PLS, pELS or DNase-H3K4me3, which overlap an ATAC-seq replicated peak in EXACTLY ONE of the twelve labels, and whose midpoint lies in no protein-coding gene body. On none of them can either rule name a host, which is the whole reason for this population.
registration.endpoint: the worm's, unchanged: the attributed gene is counted concordant when it reaches 5 transcripts per million in the element's own tissue and is higher there than in every other tissue. A gene absent from the RNA source's rows is not concordant, and the number of such genes is reported. Accessibility is not function; this endpoint says the attributed gene is expressed where the element is open, never that the element regulates it.
registration.outcome: the boundary rule against nearest TSS on the between-gene elements; percentile cluster bootstrap over 1-Mb windows; BOUNDARY_RULE_AHEAD, NEAREST_AHEAD or NO_DIFFERENCE_DETECTED
registration.second_registered_comparison: the boundary rule against the worm's gene-structure rule (simpler.domain_rule) on the same elements, with its own label, not the outcome. Two comparisons on one population, each at 95%, no correction for the pair.
registration.matched_control_and_falsifier: the matched-distance control applied to the boundary rule's gene on the population: FALSIFIED when the rule's genes match the element's tissue no more often than genes drawn at a matched distance from the element (one-sided p >= 0.05)
registration.positive_control: nearest TSS on the promoter-class elements (SCREEN's PLS, pELS and DNase-H3K4me3) against its own matched control. If it does not separate, the readout is declared unresponsive and the primary reading is withheld.
beside_deciding_nothing: the same boundaries rotated along each chromosome by one uniform offset, number and spacing kept, 1,000 draws
the two other e14.5 CTCF sets on the same elements
the elements where the two rules differ, alone
all distal elements, and the gene-structure rule against nearest TSS
labels holding 50 or more population elements
registration.power_in_advance: 2,352 of 18,407 population elements change gene under the primary boundary set, across 2,148 1-Mb clusters: about 0.74 points at 80% power, two-sided 5%, before clustering. The fly's section 11 had 216 of 3,265 and about 1.3 points.
registration.stop_rule: one run; fewer than 200 between-gene elements changing gene under the boundary rule stops it unscored and the inventory becomes the result (NO_SOURCE_QUALIFIES). The worm's and the fly's rule, unchanged.
registration.what_is_worse_here: The accessibility and the RNA come from different animals of the same strain and stage, not the same nuclei; a tissue is a mixture of cell types, so an element open in one tissue and a gene highest in that tissue can belong to different cells of it; the boundaries come from neural progenitors of embryonic neocortex and are applied to all twelve tissues, so they are stage-matched and tissue-matched to only three of them; and a domain's edges are read as its boundaries, which is the only conversion made to the boundary set.
registration.money: none; no model request, no key read, no AlphaGenome and no deletion request

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
